speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me exactly how long it has been there and if you noticed any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.

The history of an ant bite, the development of an ulcerative lesion over one month, and your significant risk factors including diabetes and immunosuppression from prior corticosteroid use for uveitis and Crohn's disease strongly point to Leishmaniasis. Can you confirm if you have ever traveled to or lived in areas where sandflies are common, such as parts of the Mediterranean, Middle East, or South America?
